News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: We will consider the call for review of LTCG tax: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
item.description: "The circumstances have changed and, therefore, the voices of concern are louder,'' she said at a media event, in reference to reports that her administration has received suggestions to review levies on long-term capital gains (LTCG) for overseas investors. "I quite appreciate that. So, I'll consider all this... Our growth is very important, where people are putting their very best, we are able to see sustained 7(%)-plus growth.''

item.title: Govt consults seed, fertiliser firms on easing regulatory hurdles
item.description: The Indian government is engaging with agricultural companies to address regulatory challenges that affect the sector. Consultations focus on updating the Seeds Act, 1966, to align with modern agricultural technology. Industry representatives have pointed out delays in approvals and licensing processes that hinder market access.

item.title: Manufacturing activity eases in Oct as new order growth drops
item.description: Manufacturing activity in India experienced a slowdown in October, decreasing from the previous month's growth. Despite this, the sector remained above its long-run average due to stronger international demand. A survey indicated that nearly 18% of manufacturers anticipated increased output over the next year, supported by fresh client inquiries.

item.title: Budget 2027: Customs duty relief on 118 goods under review
item.description: The Indian government is currently reviewing customs duty concessions applicable to 118 products set to expire. This review involves input from respective line ministries and industry stakeholders regarding these exemptions. Goods under review include materials for power projects and certain medical devices. A focus is on correcting the inverted duty structure to support local manufacturing initiatives. The outcomes of this review will influence the upcoming budget for 2027-28.

item.title: VB-G RAM G grievance redressal rules set 15-day deadline
item.description: The rules establish a multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism at the gram panchayat, block and district levels. Designated grievance redressal officers will be responsible for receiving, registering, inquiring into and disposing of complaints. Inquiries must be completed within seven working days.

item.title: Govt set to tweak MSP norms for periodic price hikes of minor forest products
item.description: The Centre is planning to restructure the minimum support price mechanism for minor forest produce. This change aims to provide periodic hikes to benefit tribal communities relying on forest produce. TERI has been tasked to study the current MSP framework and assess potential rationalization. Concerns regarding stagnant MSP rates sparking exploitation among forest-dependent communities have been raised in parliamentary discussions.

item.title: Centre's FY27 fiscal deficit may exceed Budget target by Rs 1.2 lakh crore: SBI Research
item.description: India's central government anticipates a fiscal deficit exceeding budget estimates by Rs 1.2 lakh crore in 2026-27. This increase is primarily attributed to rising fertiliser, LPG, and petroleum subsidy expenses. Strong GST growth and disinvestment receipts may not offset the expected higher deficit. In addition, SBI Research recommends a revised long-term capital gains structure to generate additional revenue.

item.title: Pakistan suffered $40 billion in economic losses due to suspension of trade with India: PIBC chief
item.description: Lahore has faced an estimated USD 40 billion in economic losses since trade with India paused in 2019. Business leaders emphasize the need for restoring these commercial ties to stimulate mutual benefits. The suspension has escalated costs for essential goods that are typically imported from India. Industries, particularly textiles and pharmaceuticals, have struggled to cope with rising transportation and sourcing expenses.

item.title: Capex key to India's growth strategy, fiscal prudence remains...: FM Sitharaman at HSBC event
India's economic pillars show 'no fragility', says Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman
item.description: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted the government's commitment to increasing capital expenditure to promote economic growth. She remarked on the importance of fiscal prudence while implementing spending strategies effectively. Sitharaman emphasized the need for public investment to enhance welfare programs and improve access to essential services. The government aims to provide comprehensive insurance coverage by 2047 to foster financial inclusion.

item.title: Capex key to India's growth strategy, fiscal prudence remains top priority: Sitharaman at HSBC event
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted the importance of capital expenditure in driving economic growth in India. She stated that government spending would be guided by fiscal discipline while encouraging private sector investment. Sitharaman noted that higher public investment has historically generated strong economic returns over time. She reassured that the Indian economy remains robust, with no sign of fragility.

item.title: Indians turn to side hustles, freelancing as non-salary income rises: ClearTax
item.description: Indians are increasingly earning from non-salary sources like trading and freelancing as reported by ClearTax. The percentage of self-filers reporting such income grew significantly from previous years. Data shows that young individuals are entering investment opportunities earlier than ever before. Additionally, women's participation in capital gains and higher income brackets has increased noticeably. This reflects a significant change in financial habits and diversification of income sources among taxpayers.

item.title: India’s manufacturing output dominated by large factories, while smaller units lag behind
item.description: India's manufacturing sector is highly fragmented, with large factories significantly outpacing small units in productivity and output. While large establishments employ most industrial workers and generate high GVA, smaller units remain burdened with debt. The productivity gap is exacerbated by limited access to technology and training for smaller factories. Additionally, women workers constitute a small fraction of the overall workforce in manufacturing.

item.title: How are equity investments taxed in India? A guide to capital gains tax
item.description: In a bid to invigorate domestic and foreign mutual fund investments, India's Securities and Exchange Board has put forth recommendations for tax concessions. These proposals are designed to boost post-tax returns, particularly as market performance has been behind that of emerging counterparts. The current capital gains tax rates are seen as a hindrance, leading to demands for a review.

item.title: Trump set for midterm test: What's in store for India, Iran, Ukraine after November 4?
item.description: US midterm election 2026: American voters' sentiments about rising prices could affect Trump's standing in trade discussions. Congressional control will determine the scrutiny over Trump's actions regarding Iran and Ukraine. India will, however, continue navigating uncertainties in trade relations regardless of the election results.

item.title: India, EU discuss FTA implementation ahead of December signing
item.description: In an effort to advance their free trade agreement, India and the European Union held pivotal discussions led by Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal, who visited Brussels for dialogues with prominent EU officials. Central to the talks were customs cooperation and trade facilitation, deemed critical for the agreement's efficacy. Additionally, industry stakeholders from the diamond sector were engaged to harness opportunities within India's expanding market.

item.title: India, EU discuss FTA implementation, customs cooperation and market access in Brussels
item.description: India and the European Union engaged in discussions regarding the implementation of their Free Trade Agreement. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held meetings with various senior European Commission officials in Brussels, focusing on market access and customs procedures. The FTA is expected to eliminate tariffs on the majority of exports from both regions. Both parties are working towards the proposed signing and full ratification of the agreement.

item.title: India factory growth slows in October, export orders jump, PMI shows
item.description: India's manufacturing growth slowed in October, with the HSBC Manufacturing PMI falling to 54.7 from 55.1 in September, as domestic demand and hiring weakened. However, export orders rose at their fastest pace in six months, providing some support to factory activity.

item.title: China’s 5,000-ton digging machines are a trade war risk to India
item.description: China is tightening export controls on tunnel-boring machines and other specialised construction equipment, raising concerns that the restrictions could disrupt India's infrastructure projects, particularly along the disputed Himalayan border.

item.title: India likely to meet FY27 fiscal deficit target despite spending pressures: Goldman Sachs
item.description: The Centre appears on track to meet the fiscal deficit target set for FY27. Strong corporate tax collections are offsetting some revenue pressures observed in the first half of the fiscal year. The government's fiscal position improved significantly in September compared to August, aided by higher direct tax revenues. Focused expenditure reallocation will be crucial in achieving the deficit goals.

item.title: GST collections jump 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October as festive demand beats high inflation and interest rates
item.description: India's GST collections in October reached ₹2.31 lakh crore, reflecting a 22.9% year-on-year increase. Strong consumption trends are indicated by rising passenger car sales and record digital payments. Power consumption also surged nearly 22% compared to last year, further emphasizing economic strength. Despite a high inflation rate of 5.5%, demand has remained robust, supporting growth forecasts. Analysts suggest this growth aligns with leading indicators of a consumption-driven economy.

item.title: One nation, many opportunities: Why India's many elections may be keeping protests peaceful
item.description: People across India are protesting peacefully, contrasting with violent agitations seen in other countries. The 'one nation, multiple elections' framework allows diverse political benefits to be shared among parties. This electoral model keeps governments accountable and responsive to public needs. Elections help to channel frustrations and enable citizens to express their concerns. As a result, the political landscape remains dynamic and participatory, fostering a sense of empowerment.

item.title: PM Modi to meet Niti Aayog leadership on Nov 5; likely to review work as govt begins shaping FY28 Budget
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to meet the new leadership of Niti Aayog on November 5. This meeting aims to establish budget priorities amidst global uncertainty and economic growth challenges. The focus will be on enhancing domestic manufacturing and creating employment opportunities. Experts from various sectors will provide insights related to India's development objectives.

item.title: CII calls for GST-like reforms in land, labour & local approvals
item.description: CII has called for extending the GST Council's approach to decriminalise offences in various sectors. This move aims to enhance ease of doing business and attract investments in land, labour, and construction. The organisation emphasizes the importance of simplifying regulatory processes across different government tiers.

item.title: Sebi to delist penny stocks: Market regulator plans AI-based surveillance of such firms
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India plans to delist companies that have no economic activity. This move aims to protect investors, especially those investing in penny stocks. The regulator highlights the potential dangers posed by such inactive companies in the market. Additionally, Sebi intends to announce compliance requirements for foreign institutional investors soon.

item.title: Mansukh Mandaviya rolls out EPFO services on WhatsApp, starts auto-settlement of small inoperative accounts
item.description: Union Labour & Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched EPFO services through WhatsApp for easier access. Subscribers can check their PF balance and transaction history conveniently using this platform. The automatic settlement for inoperative EPF accounts was also introduced, streamlining the process for beneficiaries. In total, around one lakh accounts will benefit from this initiative. The EPFO's commitment to evolve and focus on worker-centric innovations was emphasized during the celebration.

item.title: EAM Jaishankar discusses Ukraine-Russia conflict solutions amid G20 summit
item.description: India has engaged in discussions with Russia, Europe, and Ukraine regarding the ongoing conflict and its impact. These talks focused on preventing attacks on civilian shipping and restoring grain exports affected by Black Sea disruptions. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar emphasised the complexity of discussions around ceasing attacks on energy installations. Various interpretations of what constitutes energy installations have complicated these discussions.

item.title: Kashmiri apple supplies fall short of Diwali demand amid fungal outbreak
item.description: Supply of Kashmiri apples is currently inadequate due to a significant scab outbreak that has affected this year's crop. The primary concern is that a large percentage of apples arriving in markets are of lower grades. Growers are facing high production costs while receiving low returns on affected apples. Demand remains good ahead of Diwali, with higher-quality apples commanding good prices.

item.title: India's October Gross GST collections jump 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore
item.description: India's gross GST collection reached Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, representing a 22.9% increase from last year. The gross GST collected for the April-October period totaled Rs 14.78 lakh crore, showing a 13.2% growth year-on-year. Maharashtra recorded the highest revenue for October at Rs 35,150 crore, followed by Karnataka and Gujarat. Some states, including Sikkim and Ladakh, experienced significant declines in GST collections during the month.

item.title: Fuel, forex and farmers: Why India is betting big on maize
item.description: A grain that once fed chickens now fuels cars and, soon, planes. The harder question is whether Indian farms can keep up with the demand it has created.

item.title: CBDT tightens merger rules for charity trusts, imposes five-year curbs on changing objectives
item.description: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has made it mandatory for organisations merging with another registered non-profit to inform the I-T Department within a prescribed deadline, get their accounts audited and disclose the reasons for the merger. The new rules, notified on October 30, also prevent organisations with regular registration from merging with those holding provisional registration, and vice versa.

item.title: Amitabh Kant pitches for development model with rural communities as producers, innovators
item.description: Kant also stressed the need to transform rural India into centres of economic activity, innovation and entrepreneurship rather than limiting it to welfare delivery.

item.title: Centre releases states Rs 1.09 lakh cr festive boost
item.description: Uttar Pradesh received the largest allocation of ₹19,208 crore, followed by Bihar at ₹10,845 crore. Madhya Pradesh was allocated ₹8,010 crore, West Bengal ₹7,866 crore, Maharashtra ₹7,022 crore and Rajasthan ₹6,460 crore. Odisha received ₹4,819 crore and Andhra Pradesh ₹4,597 crore.

item.title: GST reforms: Easier registration for small e-commerce sellers, faster refunds to take effect Nov 1
item.description: Simplified GST registration processes will benefit small sellers using e-commerce platforms without physical presence in multiple states. The GST portal will offer user-friendly interfaces and clearer documentation requirements for registration applications. Automatic sanctioning of full refund claims for excess balance in electronic cash ledgers will expedite the refund process. Flexibility in post-supply discount taxation will support industries with volume-based incentives and trade schemes.

item.title: India extends cotton import duty exemption till December 31
item.description: The Indian government has extended the customs duty exemption on cotton imports to December 31. This decision aims to support the textile industry by ensuring adequate raw material availability. The waiver allows greater flexibility for manufacturers to source inputs at reduced costs. Domestic cotton prices have remained firm due to production concerns, prompting this extension. The move is expected to strengthen Indian textiles in both domestic and international markets.

item.title: Commerce ministry sets up committee for better utilisation of RELIEF initiative for exporters
item.description: The commerce ministry has established a six-member committee to enhance the RELIEF initiative for exporters. This initiative aims to mitigate challenges posed by rising freight costs and insurance premiums. The committee includes officials from various government departments working to improve fund utilization. It will assess the implementation of the initiative and recommend measures for better uptake. The overall goal is to support exporters during trade disruptions in crucial regions.

item.title: Indian households shifting spending towards non-food items, services as consumption patterns evolve: Report
item.description: Indian household consumption is likely to become increasingly diversified, with spending gradually moving beyond food essentials towards non-food products and services, as changing dietary preferences and household structures reshape consumption patterns, according to an SBI Research report.

item.title: Karnataka sugarcane growers stage demo to press for their demands, district officials impose restrictions
item.description: Farmers in North Karnataka are intensifying their protest over the procurement price of sugarcane and other related issues. They staged blockades and sit-ins across several locations including Belagavi and Dharwad. The farmers are demanding a fair price of Rs 5,500 per tonne for sugarcane and other reforms. Local administrations have imposed prohibitory orders to prevent further protests on highways.

item.title: 'Took stock of our bilateral cooperation': EAM Jaishankar meets US Secy of State Rubio on sidelines of G20
item.description: S Jaishankar held a bilateral meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Atlanta. The meeting focused on enhancing India-US cooperation and addressing geopolitical issues. Jaishankar emphasized that military solutions are not viable for resolving global challenges. Rubio also highlighted the importance of protecting economic and maritime security during the discussions. The G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting concluded with crucial dialogues on international economic stability.

item.title: Govt extends customs duty exemption on cotton imports till December 31
item.description: The Indian government has announced an extension of the customs duty exemption on cotton imports until December 31, 2026. This move aims to improve the availability of raw materials for the textile and apparel industry. The extension supports Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) while easing input cost pressures for manufacturers.

item.title: EAM Jaishankar slams sanctions, chokepoints disrupting global energy trade, holding prices hostage
item.description: S Jaishankar highlighted the challenges posed by disruptions in global oil supplies during the G20 meeting. He pointed out that the current energy crisis results from unpredictability and significant disruptions. Jaishankar emphasized the need for the G20 to ensure that energy markets remain open and predictable. He also mentioned India's efforts in critical minerals and the necessity for reliable energy supplies.

item.title: India-Brazil bilateral trade set to reach $20 bn with focus on critical minerals, AI, defence: Envoy
item.description: Brazil's Ambassador to India highlighted growing trade relations, expecting bilateral trade to reach USD 20 billion soon. The partnership encompasses critical sectors such as defence, energy, and pharmaceuticals, promoting economic engagement. Both nations aim to deepen cultural ties, celebrating the centenary of musician Antonio Carlos Jobim in 2027. Recent political visits strengthened commitments toward technological and economic cooperation in multilateral forums.

item.title: Fiscal deficit in H1 rises to 42.1% of FY27 target on higher capex, subsidies
item.description: By September 2026, the Centre's fiscal deficit had escalated to ₹7.14 lakh crore, exceeding last year's figures. This increase is fueled by a 10.7% rise in total expenditure, largely a result of heightened capital spending and food subsidies, while petroleum subsidies sharply declined. Gross tax revenue, however, saw a modest growth of 6.1%, even with lower excise duty collections attributed to tax reforms.

item.title: Niti Aayog's Lahiri flags growth risks in case of further monetary policy tightening
item.description: In India, it's essential for policymakers to harmonize growth output with inflation expectations. Niti Aayog’s Ashok Lahiri pointed out the importance of addressing inflation alongside job creation. He urged banks to play a pivotal role in linking enterprises with financial support and investment options. To capitalize on its natural resources, West Bengal must focus on industry attraction, while effective land acquisition and good infrastructure remain key for business development.

item.title: RBI deliberates economic risks at 625th Central Board meeting chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India conducted its 625th Central Board meeting under Governor Sanjay Malhotra. The board reviewed economic conditions and potential risks facing India’s economy while evaluating the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation’s activities. Additionally, the board members participated in the Integrity Pledge as part of Vigilance Week 2026. Deputy Governors and other board members contributed to the discussions during the meeting.

item.title: India's services trade surplus rises to $53.39 billion in Q2
item.description: The country received $113.029 billion under this head during the three months while it paid $59.637 billion, the data showed. September saw the biggest surplus at $19.208 billion while it was $17.647 billion and $16.537 billion in July and August respectively.

item.title: India’s FTAs to open access to $85 trillion market; Piyush Goyal urges exporters to go global
item.description: India's trade agreements are expected to provide exporters preferential access to markets with a combined GDP of $85 trillion, covering 76% of the global economy, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said. He urged businesses to expand internationally, improve product quality and build global brands as India pursues additional trade pacts.

item.title: CBIC holds outreach programme in Chandigarh to discuss GST 2.0 reforms with taxpayers
item.description: More than 200 taxpayers and industry representatives participated in an outreach programme with CBIC leadership. The engagement aimed to discuss implementation of reforms from the 57th GST Council meeting. Key reforms include a higher threshold for criminal prosecution and improved processes for tax refunds and registration. This initiative underscores the Finance Ministry's commitment to transparency and stakeholder engagement. The implemented reforms are set to take effect from April 1, 2027.

item.title: India PE/VC investments jump 45% to $7 billion in September, highest in over two years
item.description: Private equity and venture capital investments in India saw significant growth in September 2026. The total investment reached USD 7 billion, marking a substantial increase from August. Large-value deals accounted for 76% of the total investments during the July-September quarter. Despite this growth, the number of deals declined compared to last year. Investors are expected to remain cautious amid economic challenges and inflation pressures.

item.title: India’s forex reserves fall $1.2 billion to $719.74 billion as of October 24
item.description: India’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $1.2 billion to $719.74 billion in the week ended October 24, according to the RBI. The decline followed a sharper $5 billion drop in the previous week, when reserves stood at $721.02 billion, indicating continued pressure on the country's foreign exchange kitty.
